adversarial_case_ref: packet 06-naga-claim-ledger.md, Deliverable #2: 'Bitemporal fields and queries: "what was true at date X?" and "what did Nuzantara believe at date Y?"'
expected_behavior: This fixture is a worked example distinguishing the two queries the deliverable names. 'What was true at date X' (a valid-time query) filters on time.valid_from <= X < time.valid_to (or valid_to IS NULL). 'What did Nuzantara believe at date Y' (a system-time query) filters on time.recorded_at <= Y, then picks the highest recorded_at among survivors. The two queries below give DIFFERENT answers for the same claim family and the same date, which is the point: a system that only implements one of the two axes cannot answer both questions correctly.

revisions.note: SYNTHETIC — 'the KITAS renewal fee is IDR 2,000,000', valid Jan-Jul 2026 (a scheduled interim rate before a mid-year revision already announced in the same regulation).

SYNTHETIC — 'the KITAS renewal fee is IDR 2,500,000', valid from Jul 2026 onward. BOTH revisions were recorded_at the SAME instant (2025-12-15) because the source regulation announced both rates in one document at once.

queries.question: What did Nuzantara believe about the Aug-2026 rate, as of 2025-11-01 (before either revision was recorded)?
queries.expected_value: no belief — abstain, both revisions recorded_at 2025-12-15 which is after this query instant
